summary: Low-priority webhook clients receive persistent 429s after priority-bandit rollout; throttle headers inconsistent
description:
Issue summary: After BrightCart enabled the 'priority-bandit' routing feature to weight background webhooks lower than interactive traffic, a subset of their low-priority webhook workers started receiving sustained 429 responses. Throttle response headers are inconsistent (sometimes report remaining=0, sometimes omit headers).

Impact: BrightCart reports degraded processing of background webhooks (order-fulfillment retry callbacks). Approx 18% of callbacks fail with 429s over 6 hours, causing retry storms and delayed downstream processing. This is customer-facing (dedicated pool) and causing backlog growth in their systems.

Environment: Dedicated pool for BrightCart (org ID: org-brightcart), production us-west region. Traffic pattern: 250 webhook workers across 4 hosts, each opening 8 persistent HTTP/2 connections and issuing short POSTs (~600B payload) at ~1qps per worker. Priority-bandit was enabled at 2026-03-09 22:15 PDT.

Observed: Persistent 429s for endpoints /v1/webhook/recv from the same API key; headers inconsistent: sometimes X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, sometimes no X-RateLimit-* headers; Retry-After values vary between numeric seconds and RFC1123 timestamps. Console shows route-level burst pool configured (burst_pool_id=bg-webhook-burst) but metrics show route weight w_bg=0.1 and tenant-level token refill unchanged.

Expected: Low-priority routes should get separated burst capacity and stable, documented throttle headers with Retry-After in seconds. 429s should be queued and smoothed rather than persistent across all workers.

Temporary workaround attempted by customer: reduced worker concurrency from 8 to 2 and added exponential backoff; this reduced immediate error rate but backlog remains.

Relevant links: Slack thread #support-brightcart (https://slack.redwood/support-brightcart/p12345), console dashboard: https://console.redwood/teams/org-brightcart/metrics?panel=rate-limiter
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Enabled priority-bandit with configuration: {route: '/v1/webhook/recv', priority: low, burst_pool: 'bg-webhook-burst', weight: 0.1}
2) Start 200 short-lived workers each maintaining 4 HTTP/2 streams to gateway and sending 1req/s
3) Observe 429 responses within 5-20 minutes, throttle headers inconsistent across responses
4) Scale worker concurrency down and observe partial mitigation
logs:
Sample 429 response at 2026-03-10T02:34:12Z from 10.14.22.101:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1710159252
Retry-After: 10
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"throttle"}}

Sample 429 at 2026-03-10T02:37:03Z from 10.14.22.102:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 02:38:10 GMT
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded"}}

Gateway logs show repeated token_reassign events and burst_pool_exhausted for bg-webhook-burst starting 2026-03-09T22:20:00Z. Metric snapshot: route_bg-webhook-burst.tokens_in_use=98, pool_capacity=100, tenant_tokens_free fluctuating between 200-400.
investigation_notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Route-level burst pool accounting is double-counting requests when HTTP/2 multiplexing reassigns streams across connections, causing pool to appear exhausted while tokens exist at tenant-level.
- Hypothesis 2: Priority-bandit weight calculation produced an unintended route weight floor, causing the route to be starved after a refill epoch shift (we saw refill epoch shift at 2026-03-09T22:18:45Z).
- Hypothesis 3: A header normalization change in edge proxy removed X-RateLimit-* headers for some connection reuse patterns.
Actions taken so far:
- Pulled gateway traces for two affected hosts and correlated token assignment ids (TA-ids) -> found TA-ids being recycled across streams, logged to /var/log/rate-limiter/ta-recycle.log.
- Replayed representative traffic in staging against the same priority-bandit config; reproduced inconsistent headers when HTTP/2 connection affinity set to "pool" rather than "sticky".
- Opened quick rollback flag for priority-bandit (flag PR: github.com/redwood-inference/flags/pull/312) and staged a canary to 5% for 10 minutes.
comments: Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-10: Created ticket after customer reported high 429 rate for background webhooks following priority-bandit enablement. Customer provided request/response samples and console screenshots.

SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-10: Picked up ticket. Initial hypothesis: burst pool accounting under HTTP/2 multiplexing. Requested gateway debug logs (collected, attached). Scheduled deeper trace correlation.

Customer (BrightCart - Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Confirming we rolled the feature at 22:15 and saw error spike within 5 minutes. We can accept a short canary rollback window. Critical: we need clear guidance on proper burst_pool sizing for webhook fleets.

SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-11: Reproduced header omission locally when connection affinity set to 'pool'. Opening bug for edge-proxy header normalization (INT-998802 opened). Canary rollback started at 2026-03-11T16:40Z to 5% of dedicated hosts.

Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-12: Customer reports reduced 429s after rollback canary but still sees occasional inconsistencies; escalating to platform team for permanent fix. Advised customer to temporarily set HTTP/2 streams to 'sticky' affinity and increase burst_pool capacity by +30%.
resolution:
(ongoing) Mitigation: Canary rollback of priority-bandit reduced error-rate to baseline on canary hosts. Temporary recommendation given: set HTTP/2 affinity to sticky and increase bg-webhook-burst pool capacity by 30%.
Next steps: platform engineers to fix edge-proxy header normalization bug (INT-998802) and update burst accounting to be stream-aware. Plan: patch in 2-week sprint, validate with BrightCart test harness, then re-enable priority-bandit behind a staged rollout and observability gates. Customer follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-14.
resolution_notes: Patch candidate: edge-proxy will stop stripping X-RateLimit headers when connection ID changes (PR referenced in related_github_prs). Rate-limiter change: add per-stream token lock to prevent TA-id reuse across multiplexed streams. Postmortem doc template: confluence.redwood.internal/display/INC/Bandit+Refill+Drift+Postmortem
